summary: Reynolds County wood fire tower: built by the CCC by 1941, a new tower erected in 1973, and still listed as existing infrastructure in 2017.

facts.design: Four-legged wood tower with an observation cabin (1963 survey description)
facts.agency: Missouri Department of Conservation (formerly Missouri Conservation Commission)
facts.status_note: Last listed as existing infrastructure in a 2017 management plan. No newer source found.

access.note: Reached through Logan Creek Conservation Area. No source says whether the tower cab is open to climbers.

events.note: Wooden tower completed by the Civilian Conservation Corps for the Conservation Commission; a 1941 newspaper gives 68 feet to the lookout floor.
Annual reports record a new fire tower erected at Panther Hill. The sources do not say what became of the 1941 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Heights differ: 66 feet planned in 1940; 68 feet to the lookout floor in the 1941 newspaper; about 60 feet overall in the 1963 survey; 65 feet in a later recollection. The 1941 and 1963 figures measure different things. The record's 20.1 m equals the 66-foot planned height. No source gives a height for the tower standing today.

sources.title: Shooting the Smoke
sources.publisher: Missouri Department of Conservation (Missouri Conservationist, July 2022)

sources.title: 2017 Logan Creek Conservation Area Management Plan

notes_for_editor: Heights disagree across sources (68 ft to floor in 1941, 66 ft planned in 1940, about 60 ft overall in 1963, 65 ft in a recollection). Record height_m 20.1 equals the 66-ft planned figure; a human should decide the height field. The 1973 erection is not described in design or height, and the sources do not say whether the 1941 tower survives. Status rests on the 2017 plan; no newer source was found. A Facebook post from the Missouri Conservation History page could not be read. Not on NHLR or FFLOS in our caches. Climbing status unknown; the story advises a ground-level look unless signs say otherwise. The 1938 and 1943 acreage figures on the page differ, which is not in the story.
